name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Adopt the dual-log system with a write-through checksum plus a background reconciliation job. This guarantees no lost or corrupted transcripts while keeping the system simple enough for non-engineers to trust. The trade-off is a small increase in storage and compute, but the reliability gain is worth it. Content team owns the checksum and reconciliation job.

name: Scriv
text: The dual-log system with write-through checksum and background reconciliation still risks silent corruption if the checksum itself fails or the reconciliation job misses edge cases—like when a transcript is split across two logs during a crash. A better alternative is to switch to a single append-only log with a monotonic sequence number; it’s simpler, harder to corrupt, and the sequence number makes reconciliation trivial. The lead should run a controlled test: force a crash mid-write, then verify the transcript survives intact with no manual intervention.
